sentences.text: Kiangyousteus is an extinct genus containing only one species, the Kiangyousteus yohii.
Fossils of this animal were found in the Guanwu Formation in Sichuan province, south-western China.
Professor S. H. Yoh of Peking University discovered the fossils in 1953 in the Jiangyou district of Sichuan Province.
The genus name Kiangyousteus honors the Jiangyou district where the fossils were found, and the group was formally described by Liu in 1955.
Kiangyousteus is classified in the class Placodermi, with its parent group being Pachyosteomorphi. It is a dunkleosteid belonging to the family Dunkleosteidae.
Kiangyousteus lived during the Middle Devonian, specifically the Givetian stage, between 387.95 and 382.31 million years ago.
A 2016 study suggests that the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade separate from Dunkleosteoidea is in doubt.
